about: Checks the judge before its scores are trusted. Each pair has a good output and a deliberately bad one for the same input, scored with the same criteria the task uses. The judge passes a pair when the good output scores at least 0.75, the bad one below 0.5.

pairs.good: How would you make sure two different long URLs never get the same short code?
pairs.bad: Great answer, thanks! Can you tell me more about databases in general? Also, what's your favourite programming language?
pairs.bad_because: Praise, two questions, and neither probes the gap in the answer

pairs.good: Strong on operating systems (all four deadlock conditions, prevention by lock ordering) and solid on system design, though capacity estimates were missing. Networking needs work: the candidate knew TCP is reliable but not why (handshake, sequencing, congestion control). Databases were the weakest area: indexing was confused with row numbering. Focus next on how TCP guarantees delivery and how B-tree indexes work.
pairs.bad: An outstanding interview. The candidate excelled in every area, including an impressive deep dive into Kubernetes networking and React performance, and is clearly ready for a senior role.
pairs.bad_because: Invents topics (Kubernetes, React) and hides the weak networking and databases results
Invents an employer, a degree, titles and metrics; vague bullets

pairs.good: {"summary": "A solid mechanical design resume (SolidWorks, CATIA, ANSYS FEA, GD&T) but thin for a robotics software role: the only programming shown is MATLAB and Excel VBA.", "strengths": ["Hands-on CAD and FEA experience on real brake assemblies at Tata Motors", "Automation mindset shown by the Excel VBA bill-of-materials reports", "Quality background (Six Sigma Green Belt)"], "weaknesses": ["No C++ or Python, the core languages of robotics software", "No ROS, control or perception work", "Bullets lack measurable results"], "suggestions": ["Build and publish a small ROS 2 project, for example simulating a robot arm with a CAD model you designed", "Learn Python and port one MATLAB analysis to it", "Quantify the VBA automation, e.g. hours saved per report", "Retitle the summary toward mechatronics to bridge the two fields"]}
pairs.bad: {"summary": "An excellent robotics software resume with strong Python, ROS and C++ experience.", "strengths": ["Extensive ROS experience", "Strong C++ skills", "Great team player"], "weaknesses": ["Could use a nicer font", "Resume is slightly long", "Add a photo"], "suggestions": ["Use more action verbs", "Make it look more modern", "Proofread it"]}
pairs.bad_because: Claims Python, ROS and C++ the resume never mentions; generic advice; ignores the real gaps
